# Native function argument loan

The contract borrows the final non-receiver argument of an actual native call,
including ordinary, deferred and spawned call records. It does not certify
invocation. The query authenticates call membership, complete argument layout
and operand custody, function source ownership, representation changes and
closure bindings before lending the source function and original value.

Malformed input returns the strongest Core identity and zero observation.
Opaque, merged, nil, imported or synthetic targets supply no local source loan.
The existing Primitive function-owner helper remains authoritative; retained
ordinary-clone and genuine-instantiation proof is reused when its bytes match.
Canonical identity of fabricated generic-instance clones is not certified.

Ratchets include actual invalid-call panic recovery, source targets, schema
shape, native signature causes, capture mismatches, call-kind loans, finite
semantic mutation cases and fixed memory at 32 and 8193 native arguments.
The patches change one load-bearing fact each. Their exact native commands,
source inputs, failed assertions and output digests are retained in the owning
Mac scratch warehouse. Build errors and fixture failures are not causal proof.

Compiler construction is a separately owned whole-unit operation. The query
retains no argument/function population and imposes no input quota. Benchmark
and fuzz runs are serial 3-second development evidence. Independent acceptance
belongs to the user.
